userStories.title: Add shared webhook signature and freshness primitives
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add pure signing, signature comparison and timestamp freshness functions for outbound and inbound CI webhooks.

**Motivation** — A signed timestamp makes the freshness window enforceable and the delivery id tamper-evident.

**Approach** — **Signed string.** `<timestamp>.<deliveryId>.<body>`, joined with `.`, where `<timestamp>` is the header's text exactly as sent, `<deliveryId>` is the delivery id header's text and `<body>` is the raw request body. The signature header value has the v1 shape `sha256=<lower-case hex>`.

**Timestamp.** Decimal Unix seconds, 1 to 12 digits, no sign, no fraction. Fresh means the absolute difference between now and the timestamp is at most 300 seconds (`WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_SEC`), in both directions. Not configurable.

Use HMAC-SHA256 keyed by `secret`: v1 signs only the body, v2 signs the joined string. Compare signature strings timing-safely, returning false on byte-length mismatch. Use independent HMAC results and a fixed `nowMs` in the new unit spec; this story changes no existing test.

**Scope** — In: `webhook-security/webhook-signature.ts` and its unit spec. Out: config, outbound and inbound wiring, route documentation, configurable tolerance, and delivery-ID character restrictions.

**Interface**
```ts
// webhook-security/webhook-signature.ts
export const WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_SEC = 300;
export function signatureV1(secret: string, body: string): string;                       // 'sha256=<hex>'
export function signatureV2(secret: string, timestamp: string, deliveryId: string, body: string): string;
export function signaturesMatch(expected: string, received: string): boolean;            // timing-safe, false on length mismatch
export function isFreshTimestamp(timestamp: string, nowMs: number): boolean;
```
acceptanceCriteria: When `signatureV1('s3cret', '{"a":1}')` is called, then it returns `sha256=` followed by the lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 of `{"a":1}` keyed by `s3cret`.
When `signatureV2('s3cret', '1700000000', 'd-1', '{"a":1}')` is called, then it returns `sha256=` followed by the lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 of `1700000000.d-1.{"a":1}` keyed by `s3cret`.
When `signatureV2` is called with `d-2` instead of `d-1` and the other AC-2 inputs unchanged, then it returns a value different from the AC-2 result.
When `signaturesMatch(x, x)` compares an equal `sha256=` string, then it returns `true`.
When `signaturesMatch('sha256=abc', 'sha256=ab')` is called, then it returns `false` without throwing.
When `signaturesMatch('sha256=abc', 'sha256=abd')` is called, then it returns `false`.
When `isFreshTimestamp(String(nowSec - 300), nowSec * 1000)` is called, then it returns `true`.
When `isFreshTimestamp(String(nowSec + 300), nowSec * 1000)` is called, then it returns `true`.
When `isFreshTimestamp(String(nowSec - 301), nowSec * 1000)` is called, then it returns `false`.
When `isFreshTimestamp(String(nowSec + 301), nowSec * 1000)` is called, then it returns `false`.
When `isFreshTimestamp('1700000000.5', 1700000000000)` is called, then it returns `false`.
When `isFreshTimestamp('', 1700000000000)` is called, then it returns `false`.
When `isFreshTimestamp('+1700000000', 1700000000000)` is called, then it returns `false`.
When `isFreshTimestamp('1700000000000', 1700000000000)` is called with the 13-digit timestamp, then it returns `false`.

routing.reasoning: A small pure module and unit spec with standard Node crypto; cryptography requires strict test isolation.

suggestedCriteria: When a timestamp contains a trailing newline after otherwise fresh decimal digits, then `isFreshTimestamp` returns `false`.
When `signatureV2` signs a timestamp with a leading zero, then the resulting HMAC covers that leading zero.

userStories.title: Register deployment-wide webhook signature switches
acceptanceCriteria: When neither `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_V1_ENABLED` nor `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2` is set, then `webhookSignatureConfig().v1Enabled` is `true`.
When neither `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_V1_ENABLED` nor `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2` is set, then `webhookSignatureConfig().ciRequireV2` is `false`.
When `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_V1_ENABLED=false`, then `webhookSignatureConfig().v1Enabled` is `false`.
When `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_V1_ENABLED=FALSE`, then `webhookSignatureConfig().v1Enabled` is `false`.
When `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2=true`, then `webhookSignatureConfig().ciRequireV2` is `true`.
When `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2=TRUE`, then `webhookSignatureConfig().ciRequireV2` is `true`.

userStories.title: Sign outbound webhook attempts with timestamp and delivery ID
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Send v2 headers on every outbound delivery attempt while retaining the v1 header by default.

**Motivation** — Nothing in the signed bytes binds the message to a time.

**Approach** — **Outbound timestamp per attempt.** The handler stamps the time of each send as `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)`, so an outbox retry carries a fresh timestamp and passes a receiver's tolerance. `X-Koda-Delivery-Id` keeps its content-hash derivation, so a retry keeps the same id for receiver dedupe.

**Signed string.** `<timestamp>.<deliveryId>.<body>`, joined with `.`, where `<timestamp>` is the header's text exactly as sent, `<deliveryId>` is the delivery id header's text and `<body>` is the raw request body. The signature header value has the v1 shape `sha256=<lower-case hex>`.

Read `IWebhookSignatureConfig` through `ConfigService.get(WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG)`, defaulting `v1Enabled` to true when the namespace is undefined. Compute signatures with `signatureV2` and `signatureV1` using the exact body passed to unchanged `OutboundHttpClient.post(url, headers, body)`. Preserve `Content-Type`, `X-Koda-Event`, skipping missing or inactive hooks, and the transport's exception behavior. Add a key-specific ConfigService stub to `webhook-delivery.handler.spec.ts`, update the exact header assertion to the six-header default, and independently recompute v2 from the posted inputs to prove the call site is wired. Add a stub returning undefined to `webhook-delivery.seam.spec.ts`, leaving its transport assertions unchanged.

**Scope** — In: outbound handler signing, headers and tests. Out: shared primitive/config authoring, inbound verification, receiver verification code, secret rotation, v1 code removal, and changing delivery-ID derivation.

**Interface** — `constructor(webhookRepo: PrismaWebhookRepository, http: OutboundHttpClient, config: ConfigService)`; `handle` also sends `X-Koda-Timestamp` and `X-Koda-Signature-V2`, and sends `X-Koda-Signature` only when `v1Enabled` is true.
acceptanceCriteria: When `WebhookDeliveryHandler.handle` sends with the clock at `2026-11-19T12:00:00Z`, then the posted `X-Koda-Timestamp` is the string `'1795089600'`.

When `handle` posts a delivery, then `X-Koda-Signature-V2` equals `sha256=` plus the hex HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the webhook secret of the posted `X-Koda-Timestamp`, `.`, posted `X-Koda-Delivery-Id`, `.`, and posted body.

When `handle` sends with `ConfigService.get(WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG)` returning `{ v1Enabled: true, ciRequireV2: false }`, then `X-Koda-Signature` equals `sha256=` plus the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body keyed by the webhook secret.

When `handle` sends with `ConfigService.get` returning `{ v1Enabled: false, ciRequireV2: false }` for `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG` and `undefined` for any other key, then it posts no `X-Koda-Signature` header.
When `handle` sends in the AC-4 setup, then it still posts `X-Koda-Signature-V2`.
When `handle` sends with `ConfigService.get(WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG)` returning `undefined`, then it posts `X-Koda-Signature`.
When `handle` is called twice with the same webhook, event and payload 100 seconds apart, then both calls post the same `X-Koda-Delivery-Id`.
When `handle` is called twice in the AC-7 setup, then the posted `X-Koda-Timestamp` values are 100 seconds apart.
When `handle` sends with the default config, then it posts exactly `Content-Type`, `X-Koda-Event`, `X-Koda-Delivery-Id`, `X-Koda-Signature`, `X-Koda-Timestamp` and `X-Koda-Signature-V2`.

routing.reasoning: An existing handler and two test fixtures consume established seams; outbound signing is cryptography.

modifiedFiles.reason: its `new WebhookDeliveryHandler(webhookRepo, http)` factory gains a third `ConfigService` stub argument whose `get` answers the signature config only for `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG` (default `undefined`, so v1 stays on), and its exact `expect(headers).toEqual({...})` header set gains `X-Koda-Timestamp` and `X-Koda-Signature-V2`; the invariant that replaces it is the six-header set of US-003 AC-9.
its `new WebhookDeliveryHandler(makeWebhookRepo(url), client)` construction gains a third `ConfigService` stub argument answering `undefined`; its transport assertions are unchanged.

suggestedCriteria: When `OutboundHttpClient.post` rejects with `WebhookDeliveryError('http_5xx')`, then `WebhookDeliveryHandler.handle` rejects with that same error instance, preserving existing transport error propagation.

userStories.title: Verify inbound CI webhook v2 without fallback on failure
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Verify signed timestamps and delivery IDs before processing CI webhook payloads, with v1 fallback only when v2 is absent and not required.

**Motivation** — A signed timestamp makes the freshness window enforceable and the delivery id tamper-evident.

**Approach** — **Inbound decision order** (after the project lookup, before payload validation):
1. `x-ci-signature-v2` present (any value, including empty): verify v2 only. `x-ci-delivery` and `x-ci-timestamp` must both be present, the timestamp must be fresh and the v2 HMAC must match; otherwise 401. The v1 header is ignored.
2. `x-ci-signature-v2` absent and `ciRequireV2` true: 401.
3. Otherwise: verify v1 exactly as today.

Every refusal is the existing `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')`, the same 401 as an unknown slug or a bad signature, so the route reveals neither which slugs exist nor which check failed. A refusal happens before `WebhookReplayGuard.assertFresh`, so a refused delivery does not consume its delivery id. The guard's `Date` window and delivery-id dedupe are unchanged.

**Timestamp.** Decimal Unix seconds, 1 to 12 digits, no sign, no fraction. Fresh means the absolute difference between now and the timestamp is at most 300 seconds (`WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_SEC`), in both directions. Not configurable.

**Signed string.** `<timestamp>.<deliveryId>.<body>`, joined with `.`, where `<timestamp>` is the header's text exactly as sent, `<deliveryId>` is the delivery id header's text and `<body>` is the raw request body. The signature header value has the v1 shape `sha256=<lower-case hex>`.

Use unchanged `signedBytesOf(request: InboundWebhookRequest): string` for the raw body, and leave `WebhookReplayGuard.assertFresh(input: ReplayCheckInput): Promise<void>` and `forget(input)` unchanged, including the existing SYSTEM/ci context. Use `signatureV1`, `signatureV2`, `signaturesMatch` and `isFreshTimestamp`. Read `ConfigService.get(WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG)` and fall back to `ciRequireV2: false` when undefined. Add a `ConfigService` provider stub in `ci-webhook.controller.spec.ts`: undefined by default, configured values only under the correct namespace. Independently compute the v2 HMAC over the exact timestamp text, delivery-ID text and raw body for the successful controller call and the signed/sent delivery-ID mismatch. In rejection cases, keep the unrelated inputs valid so the intended failure is isolated. For wrong-secret v2, compare the exception response with the existing bad-v1 response; keep the existing v1 cases unchanged.

**Scope** — In: controller verification and header binding, config consumption and controller specs. Out: outbound behavior, OpenAPI metadata and artifact generation, route-level tests, CLI signing, deleting v1, GitHub VCS webhooks, changes to `WebhookReplayGuard` (including its `Date` window and existing within-window dedupe), preventing fallback when the v2 header is stripped while `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2` is false, configurable timestamp tolerance, delivery-ID character restrictions, and secret rotation or multiple active secrets.

**Interface** — `constructor(ciWebhookService, replayGuard, config: ConfigService)`; `handleCiWebhook(slug, request, signature?, deliveryId?, dateHeader?, timestamp?, signatureV2?)`, the two new parameters read `x-ci-timestamp` and `x-ci-signature-v2`. The existing positional parameters keep their order, so existing calls stay valid. Signature checks go through `webhook-security/webhook-signature.ts`.
acceptanceCriteria: When `CiWebhookController.handleCiWebhook` receives a fresh `x-ci-timestamp`, an `x-ci-delivery`, a matching `x-ci-signature-v2` and no `x-ci-signature`, then it calls `CiWebhookService.processCiWebhook` with the validated payload.

When `handleCiWebhook` receives a matching v2 signature and a wrong `x-ci-signature` with `ConfigService.get(WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG)` returning `{ v1Enabled: true, ciRequireV2: true }`, then it calls `processCiWebhook`.

When `handleCiWebhook` receives an `x-ci-signature-v2` computed under a different secret than the project's CI token and a valid `x-ci-signature`, then it rejects with the same `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401 as a bad v1 signature.
When `handleCiWebhook` receives a matching v2 signature over an `x-ci-timestamp` 301 seconds in the past, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `handleCiWebhook` receives a matching v2 signature over an `x-ci-timestamp` 301 seconds in the future, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `handleCiWebhook` receives `x-ci-timestamp` `abc` and an `x-ci-signature-v2` computed over it, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `handleCiWebhook` receives `x-ci-signature-v2` but no `x-ci-delivery`, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `handleCiWebhook` receives `x-ci-signature-v2` but no `x-ci-timestamp`, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.

When `ConfigService.get` returns `{ v1Enabled: true, ciRequireV2: true }` for `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG` and `undefined` for any other key, and `handleCiWebhook` receives a valid `x-ci-signature` with no `x-ci-signature-v2`, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `ConfigService.get(WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG)` returns `undefined` and `handleCiWebhook` receives a valid `x-ci-signature` with no `x-ci-signature-v2`, then it calls `processCiWebhook`.
When `handleCiWebhook` receives an empty `x-ci-signature-v2` and a valid `x-ci-signature`, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `handleCiWebhook` receives an `x-ci-signature-v2` computed over delivery ID `d-1` but receives `x-ci-delivery` `d-2`, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `handleCiWebhook` refuses the bad v2 HMAC with valid v1 from AC-3, then `WebhookReplayGuard.assertFresh` is not called.
When `handleCiWebhook` refuses the v1-only delivery from AC-9 under `ciRequireV2: true`, then `WebhookReplayGuard.assertFresh` is not called.

routing.reasoning: Changes one controller and its tests using existing seams; authentication precedence and replay ordering require strict test isolation.

modifiedFiles.reason: its `Test.createTestingModule` providers list has no `ConfigService`; it gains a `ConfigService` stub whose `get` answers `undefined` by default (v1 accepted, v2 not required) and answers the signature config only for the key `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_CFG` in the switch cases; its existing v1 cases keep passing unchanged.

suggestedCriteria: When `handleCiWebhook` receives v2 with a present timestamp that does not consist of 1–12 decimal digits, then it rejects with the `AuthException({}, 'ci_webhook')` 401.
When `handleCiWebhook` refuses a delivery at signature verification, then it does not call `WebhookReplayGuard.assertFresh`, so the refused delivery ID is not recorded.

userStories.title: Expose and verify the v2-only CI webhook HTTP contract
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the optional signature headers in the CI webhook contract, regenerate API client artifacts and verify v2-only authentication end to end.

**Motivation** — When a CI delivery carries `X-CI-Signature-V2`, a failing v2 is refused even when v1 verifies.

**Approach** — **OpenAPI.** The CI route documents `x-ci-timestamp`, `x-ci-signature-v2` and `x-ci-signature` as optional header parameters (`required: false`), each appearing once. A v2-only sender omits `x-ci-signature`. Declare each with `@ApiHeader({ name, required: false, description })` on the handler, name in lower case exactly as the `@Headers` parameter: `@nestjs/swagger` 12 merges an explicit header into the reflected parameter of the same name and `in` (`dist/explorers/api-parameters.explorer.js`), so the explicit `required: false` wins and nothing is duplicated.

Test the committed `openapi.json` DB-free using the approval contract spec's file-reading pattern. Test the real route with `bootHttpApp`, a real project `ciWebhookToken` and the raw-body delivery pattern in the audit CI webhook integration spec. Independently compute HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<deliveryId>.<body>` using the project's `ciWebhookToken`, the exact timestamp text and the exact raw JSON string sent. In the refusal case, keep the timestamp fresh and all other inputs valid, use an unused `x-ci-delivery` value, and change only the ID between the signed input and that header. Add a v2-only 200 case to `test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` alongside the unchanged v1 cases. Regenerate `openapi.json` and `apps/cli/src/generated/types.gen.ts` with `bun run generate` from the repo root; never hand-edit them.

**Scope** — In: route header contract and HTTP tests, API endpoint e2e update, regenerated OpenAPI and CLI types. Out: controller verification algorithm, docs page, CLI command behavior, and changing the OpenAPI documentation of `x-ci-delivery` and `date`, which stay documented as required.

**Interface** — `POST /api/projects/:slug/ci-webhook` (`post` at `/api/projects/{slug}/ci-webhook` in OpenAPI); `handleCiWebhook(slug, request, signature?, deliveryId?, dateHeader?, timestamp?, signatureV2?)`. The v2-only request supplies `x-ci-timestamp`, `x-ci-delivery` and `x-ci-signature-v2` over `<timestamp>.<X-CI-Delivery>.<body>`, omitting `x-ci-signature`.
acceptanceCriteria: When `POST /api/projects/:slug/ci-webhook` on the app booted by `bootHttpApp` receives a raw JSON body signed as v2 under the project's `ciWebhookToken`, a fresh `x-ci-timestamp`, an `x-ci-delivery` and no `x-ci-signature`, then it answers 200.
When the same route receives an otherwise valid v2-only request whose signature was computed over a different delivery ID than the sent `x-ci-delivery`, then it answers 401.

When the committed `openapi.json` is read DB-free as `approvals/approval-openapi.contract.spec.ts` reads it, then the `post` operation of `/api/projects/{slug}/ci-webhook` has exactly one `x-ci-signature-v2` header parameter with `required: false`.
When the same `post` operation is inspected in the AC-3 document, then it has exactly one `x-ci-timestamp` header parameter with `required: false`.
When the same `post` operation is inspected in the AC-3 document, then it has exactly one `x-ci-signature` header parameter with `required: false`.

routing.reasoning: Three Swagger header overrides span committed API and CLI artifacts plus full-app tests, and exercising raw-body authentication end to end requires strict test isolation.

modifiedFiles.reason: the api-testing rule requires endpoint changes to be reflected here; its CI webhook block gains a v2-only delivery case answering 200 next to the existing v1 cases, which keep passing unchanged.

the CI webhook operation (POST on the project ci-webhook path) gains optional `x-ci-timestamp` and `x-ci-signature-v2` header parameters and `x-ci-signature` becomes optional; regenerate with `bun run generate` from the repo root, never hand-edit.
regenerated by `bun run generate` for the same header changes on the CI webhook operation's data type; never hand-edited.

suggestedCriteria: When `POST /api/projects/:slug/ci-webhook` receives a valid v1-only delivery during the default deprecation window, then it still answers 200, as in the unchanged v1 endpoint cases.

userStories.title: Document webhook v2 for receivers and deployment operators
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Publish `docs/deployment/webhooks.md` with outbound verification, inbound CI signing and deprecation-window guidance.

**Motivation** — The window ends through environment switches (outbound v1 off, inbound v2 required).

**Approach** — **Signed string.** `<timestamp>.<deliveryId>.<body>`, joined with `.`, where `<timestamp>` is the header's text exactly as sent, `<deliveryId>` is the delivery id header's text and `<body>` is the raw request body. The signature header value has the v1 shape `sha256=<lower-case hex>`.

**Timestamp.** Decimal Unix seconds, 1 to 12 digits, no sign, no fraction. Fresh means the absolute difference between now and the timestamp is at most 300 seconds (`WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE_SEC`), in both directions. Not configurable.

**Outbound timestamp per attempt.** The handler stamps the time of each send as `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)`, so an outbox retry carries a fresh timestamp and passes a receiver's tolerance. `X-Koda-Delivery-Id` keeps its content-hash derivation, so a retry keeps the same id for receiver dedupe.

**Switches.** `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_V1_ENABLED` (boolean, default `true`) and `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2` (boolean, default `false`).

Use the sections `Outbound webhooks`, `Inbound CI webhook` and `Deprecation window`. Document the outbound headers, body-only v1 and HMAC-SHA256 v2; tell receivers to enforce the 300-second clock window and dedupe on the stable ID. For inbound CI, give the exact `<timestamp>.<X-CI-Delivery>.<body>` input using the project's CI token. State that any present v2 header, even empty, alone decides; a failed v2 signature is not rescued by v1, and v1-only requests can be accepted while v2 is not required. Explain that setting `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_V1_ENABLED=false` stops outbound v1 and `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2=true` rejects inbound deliveries without v2. Explain the v1 fallback risk when the v2 header is stripped and advise waiting until every CI sender uses v2 before requiring it.

**Scope** — In: deployment guide only. Out: runtime and generated contract changes, CLI v2 signing, and receiver-side verification code.

**Interface** — Outbound: `X-Koda-Timestamp`, `X-Koda-Signature-V2`, `X-Koda-Signature`, `X-Koda-Delivery-Id`, `X-Koda-Event`. Inbound CI: `X-CI-Timestamp`, `X-CI-Signature-V2`, `X-CI-Delivery`, `X-CI-Signature`. Both signature versions use `sha256=<hex>`.
acceptanceCriteria: When `docs/deployment/webhooks.md` is reviewed, then its `Outbound webhooks` section names `X-Koda-Timestamp`, `X-Koda-Signature-V2`, `X-Koda-Signature`, `X-Koda-Delivery-Id` and `X-Koda-Event`.
When `Outbound webhooks` describes v2, then it gives `<timestamp>.<deliveryId>.<body>` as the signed string and `sha256=<hex>` as the header value form.

When `Outbound webhooks` describes replay protection, then it tells receivers to refuse a timestamp more than 300 seconds from their clock and dedupe on `X-Koda-Delivery-Id`, which is stable across retries.

When `Inbound CI webhook` describes signing, then it names `X-CI-Timestamp`, `X-CI-Signature-V2`, `X-CI-Delivery` and `X-CI-Signature` and gives `<timestamp>.<X-CI-Delivery>.<body>` as the signed string.
When `Inbound CI webhook` describes signature precedence, then it states that a present `X-CI-Signature-V2` alone decides, so failing v2 is refused even when v1 verifies.

When `Deprecation window` describes deployment switches, then it names `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_V1_ENABLED` (default `true`) and `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2` (default `false`) and explains what each does when switched.

When `Deprecation window` describes the compatibility risk, then it states that while `CI_WEBHOOK_REQUIRE_V2` is false a captured delivery with its v2 header stripped can still pass signature verification on a valid v1 signature, so operators turn it on once every CI sender sends v2.

routing.reasoning: The binding documentation-only story records the protocol and operator guidance in one new page.
routing.noTestJustification: Adds one documentation page without changing executable behavior; verify the specified content by review.

analysis:
Goal and scope: implement the 2026-11-19 owner ruling on outbound freshness and CI intake authentication (docs/20261114-review-whole-repo.md:195, :517, :549). Koda always sends signed timestamp + delivery ID + body outbound, and CI intake verifies that form when present. Preserve v1 compatibility by default, then close the window with independent deployment switches. No database migration, new dependency, secret change, or new route is needed. The codebase-memory MCP was unavailable, so repository findings were verified with direct reads and text search.

Shared signing and time: the prior implementations already produce sha256= plus lower-case hex. The CI implementation uses Buffer byte lengths and timingSafeEqual (apps/api/src/ci-webhook/ci-webhook.controller.ts:73). Centralize both variants using Node crypto, preserve exact timestamp and delivery-ID text for signing, and parse timestamp separately for freshness. Use the exact payload string sent by the transport or captured by Fastify, not normalized JSON. The production Fastify plugin registers raw-body capture (apps/api/src/common/bootstrap/fastify-runtime.plugin.ts:25); signedBytesOf prefers the captured UTF-8 body and falls back to serialized JSON for test requests without rawBody (apps/api/src/webhook-security/inbound-webhook-request.ts:13). Pure tests should pin independent HMAC results, constant-time comparison behavior, exact skew boundaries in both directions, and invalid syntax.

Configuration: apps/api/src/app.module.ts:73 registers global ConfigService and loads config factories through the existing validate hook. Model the namespace after apps/api/src/config/retention.config.ts:36 and case-insensitive factory validation after apps/api/src/config/outbox.config.ts:27 and :49, without copying NODE_ENV-dependent defaults. The matching Joi boolean rule is at apps/api/src/config/env.validation.ts:51; validate builds a ValidationAppException with field names in the error message at :135. Keep IWebhookConfig and ConfigBridgeModule unchanged. Isolate and restore switch values in tests, including around the full-app boot, because factories read process.env during creation (apps/api/test/helpers/http-app.ts:53). A missing namespace must not be confused with failed DI or with an explicit false switch.

Outbound: apps/api/src/webhook/webhook-delivery.handler.ts:21 skips missing or inactive hooks, serializes once, derives SHA-256(webhookId:event:body) for stable dedupe, then calls post with that same body. Wire the shared signer and namespace into this handler only; compute the timestamp on each send attempt, not at enqueue. apps/api/src/webhook/webhook.module.ts:27 provides the handler and transport; apps/api/src/webhook/webhook-outbox.subscriber.ts:14 registers webhook_delivery and delegates every attempt to handle. Preserve the system-writer classification and transport error propagation; apps/api/src/webhook/outbound/outbound-http-client.ts:57 remains the transport boundary. The handler unit spec constructs the handler at apps/api/src/webhook/webhook-delivery.handler.spec.ts:61 and pins the old exact header set at :104; update that assertion to the six-header default, retain URL/body/error and skip assertions. The transport seam constructs it directly at apps/api/src/webhook/webhook-delivery.seam.spec.ts:80; add only the config stub there.
